svg.title: Family Research Counts Are Not Entitlement Proof
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-family-research-counts; chapter number: 2; title: Family Research Counts Are Not Entitlement Proof; subtitle: Separate display depth, competing identities, located relatives, and signed beneficiaries.; caption: James Tanner demonstrates FamilySearch generations; Christa Cowen separates Daniel Jones identities; Heir Hunters reports the Victor and Wearing cases; Amy Moyes on Ancestry reports signed maternal heirs in the Eileen Holmes case.; assumptions note: James Tanner, Christa Cowen, Heir Hunters, and Amy Moyes describe different units and cases. Equal minimum, maximum, and typical entries preserve each quoted count or ceiling; they do not assert a statistical distribution or typical case size.; note: Tanner's four generations are a display ceiling. Cowen's five men are competing identities, not heirs. Heir Hunters did not confirm the Wearing estate value, and Amy Moyes's eighteen signatures were a progress report.; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: Reported count; the counted item is identified in each label; bars: label: FamilySearch generation display ceiling; min: 4; max: 4; typical: 4; display: Up to 4 generations; label: Distinct Daniel Jones identities; min: 5; max: 5; typical: 5; display: 5 men distinguished; label: Victor estate heirs; min: 16; max: 16; typical: 16; display: 16 heirs sharing the reported estate; label: Eileen Holmes signed maternal heirs; min: 18; max: 18; typical: 18; display: 18 signed so far; label: Wearing investigation heirs; min: 53; max: 53; typical: 53; display: 53 heirs; estate value unconfirmed
